- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or shows recent reversal, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overcorrection lag.
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean over 30d, apply upward bias adjustment — especially if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
- If model consistently underpredicts in early days of forecast horizon (e.g., day 1–5), consider adding 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast to account for lagged sentiment effects.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with true trend; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent sentiment, 30% historical) to reduce noise.
